Most employees the model expects to remain also fall into this early-career group, so your limited overall experience actually worked in your favor. 

However, two other factors pushed more strongly toward leaving. The fact that you have received other job offers while at the company was the second most important reason, signaling that external opportunities may be pulling you away. Third, not having medical insurance in your current role also increased the likelihood of departure, as employees without coverage are more likely to look elsewhere.

Taken together, the model sees your external opportunities and lack of medical benefits as outweighing the stabilizing effect of your early-career stage.
